summary: Josh Lloyd and Eric Slater (Locked On Nets) preview the 2026/27 Brooklyn Nets. The Nets added Julius Randle, drafted Mikel Brown Jr. sixth overall, signed Moritz Wagner and Keon Ellis for veteran depth, and lost Nic Claxton and Ziaire Williams. The Nets do not control their own pick this season, so under the new lottery reform they gain nothing from tanking and plan to try to win while developing and evaluating their young players. Day'Ron Sharpe is expected to start at center, but his minutes split with Wagner is uncertain. Michael Porter Jr. is not seen as a long-term piece and could be traded within six months if he does not sign an extension. Slater sees Randle as the player who raises the team's ceiling and predicts about 28 wins, above the 24.5 over/under.

rules.text: Lottery reform should make the league more competitive overall. Fewer teams will tank and there will be fewer cheap wins against tanking teams.
rules.quote: less teams tanking. There's going to be less of those kind of cheap wins up for grabs.

rules.text: Teams that do not control their own pick (Nets, Bucks, Clippers, Pelicans, Mavericks) have no reason to tank and no downside either. They may rest players, be extra careful with injuries, or give developmental minutes late in the season.
rules.quote: no downside to them, you know, sitting guys down or being extra cautious with an injury or being extra bold

rules.text: Rookie point guards nearly all struggle in their first NBA season, so expectations for them should be tempered.
rules.quote: Understanding rookie point guards, it's one of the hardest things to do in the NBA and they nearly all struggle.

rules.text: Win totals this season will be on a different curve than last season because more teams will be trying to win under the lottery reform.
rules.quote: these win totals are kind of going to be on a different curve than what they were last season.
